Explanation: The peasants dispossessed by the Company rule and the soldiers of the disbanded armies of the kings and nawabs first laid the foundation of the Sanyas Rebellion in Bengal under the leadership of the deposed landlords and religious leaders. Questions: Who was the Finance Minister in the Interim government?
Explanation:
On 2 September 1946, an interim government was formed under Jawaharlal Nehru. Later he became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan

Questions: Which of the following persons had participated actively in the Revolt of 1857?
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: The following people actively participated in the revolt of 1857 AD. Nana Saheb participated in this movement in Kanpur, Begum Hazrat Mahal in Lucknow, Maulvi Ahmedullah in Faizabad and Bahadur Shah's wife Begum Zeenat Mahal in Delhi. Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi started the Dandi March from Sabarmati on 12 March 1930, which ended in Dandi on 6 April 1930. This came to be known as Salt Satyagraha The Dandi March organized by Gandhiji lasted for 24 days. This march was against the illegal tax imposed on salt.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who is the author of the popular song, Sarfaroshi ki Tamanna Ab Hamare Dil Mein Hai?
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: Bismil Azimabadi was a revolutionary from Bihar who wrote the ghazal “Sarfaroshi Ki Tamanna” in 1921 Although this ghazal was composed by the famou Ram Prasad Bismil. These lines of the ghazal infused new energy among the revolutionaries during the freedom struggle.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Sarfaroshi ki Tamanna Ab Hamare Dil Mein Hai

Questions: Which movement was started as a reaction to the Partition of Bengal?
Explanation: Partition of Bengal was announced on 19 July 1905 which was implemented on 16 October 1905. Swadesh movement was celebrated all over the country in protest against the partition of Bengal. In this movement, an attempt was made to cause economic loss to the imperialist British by using goods made in India and boycotting foreign goods.

Questions: Who among the following advocates had appeared for the INA trials at Delhi in 1945-46?
Explanation: Azad Hind Fauj officers Colonel Prem Sehgal, Colonel Gurubaksh Singh and Major General Shahnawaz Khan were tried jointly in 1945-46 AD, in which Bhulabhai Desai had advocated in their favor.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Where did Madam Cama unfurl india’s tricolour flag of freedom?
Explanation: Madam Bhikaji Cama hoisted the first national flag of India in Stuttgart, Germany on 22 August 1907 (7th International Congress) as a symbol of the Indian independence movement. Madam Bhikaji Cama is also called the mother of Indian independence.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which of the following pairs is correct?
Option D: Shyamji Krishna Varma - Founder of India House in Paris
Explanation:
• The first Satyagrahi to be selected for individual Satyagraha was Vinoba Bhave.
• Chittaranjan Das is known by the nickname of Deshbandhu.

Questions: Which day was declared as 'Purna Swaraj Day' by the Indian National Congress?
Explanation: In the year 1929, during the Lahore session of the Congress, socialist leader Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the national flag on the banks of the Ravi River in Lahore and on 26 January 1930, it was announced to celebrate Purna Swaraj Day by the Indian National Congress. After independence, this day was adopted as Republic Day (26 January 1950 AD).
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The dual system of governance in Bengal was enforced by
Explanation: Diarchy system was implemented in Bengal by Robert Clive in the year 1765 AD. It was abolished by Warren Hastings in 1772. Under this, the British kept the rights with themselves and imposed the duties on the Indians. Warren Hastings was the first Governor General of Bengal. He was the only Governor General who faced an impeachment trial.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who among the following participated in the Parliament of Religions held at Chicago in 1893?
Explanation: Swami Vivekananda represented India in the Religion Conference held in Chicago (America) on 11 September 1893. Representatives of religions from all over the world participated in this conference. Swami Vivekananda's childhood name was Narendra Dutt. He is considered the spiritual guru of India. He established Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 AD. “National Youth Day” is celebrated on his birthday, 12th January.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who established Swaraj Party in 1923?
Explanation: Swaraj Party was founded by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru in 1923 AD. After the end of the noncooperation movement, there was dissatisfaction among various leaders of the Congress, due to this dispute, Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das separated and formed the Swaraj Party. Its main objective was to enter the legislative assemblies and criticize the policies of the government.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who wrote the famous play Neel Darpan in which oppression of indigo farmers is displayed?
Explanation: The creator of the play Neel Darpan was Dinbandhu Mitra. The play is based on the Indigo Rebellion (1859). In this the plight of indigo farmers has been discussed. Neel Darpan was translated into English by Madhusudan Dutt. The incident of Indigo rebellion took place in Nadia district of Bengal, whose main leaders were Digambara Biswas and Vishnu Biswas.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The famous Battle of Wandiwash in 1760 was fought by the British against whom?
Explanation: On January 22, 1760, the Battle of Wandiwash took place between the British and the French. This was a decisive battle in which the French army was defeated. Eyre coote led the English army in the battle of Wandiwash. After this war, it was decided that India would be ruled by the British. Wandiwash is in Tamil Nadu.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which of the following Acts introduced separate electorates system in India?
Explanation: The first electoral college in India was introduced by the Indian Council Act, 1909. This act is also known as Morley-Minto Reforms. Under this Act, the system of separate electorate was adopted for the first time in India.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Kol Mutiny of 1831 under Buddho Bhagat took place in which of the following regions?
Explanation: The Kol rebellion took place in the areas of Singhbhum. The main leaders of this rebellion were Buddho Bhagat and Madari Mahato. This rebellion took place in 1831 – 32 AD.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: In which of the following colleges Gandhiji had studied?
Explanation:
Gandhiji's early education took place in Rajkot. After passing matriculation, he studied at Shyamal Da College, Bhavnagar, after which he went to England fo further studies.

Questions: Who was the first Governor-General of India?
Answer: (E) None of the above/More than one o the above
Explanation: The first Governor General of India was Lord William Bentinck. By the Act of 1833 AD, the Governor General of Bengal started being called the Governor General of India. Its reign was from 1828 – 1835 AD. During his reign works like social reforms and educational reforms were done. The practice of Sati was ended in 1829 AD by the efforts of Raja Rammohan Roy.

Questions: Who was the founder of British Empire in India?
Explanation: Lord Clive is considered as the founder of the British Empire in India. After winning the Battle of Plassey on 23 June 1757, it indirectly laid the foundation of the British Empire in India.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Where from the Revolution of 1857 started first?
Explanation: The revolt of 1857 started from Meerut on 10 May 1857. The rebellion of 1857 AD was the first reaction of organized resistance against the East India Company. The influence of this rebellion gradually spread to other areas of the country. The Governor General of India at the time of this rebellion was Lord Canning, whose tenure was (1856–1862).
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the leader of Munda Revolt?
Explanation: The leader of the Munda rebellion was Birsa Munda. The expansion area of this rebellion was South Bihar and Jharkhand. This rebellion is also known as Ulgulan rebellion. At present, Birsa Munda has the status of God in the tribal society and due to his thoughts and actions, he is also known as 'Dharti Aaba'.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Who established the 'Arya Samaj'?
Explanation: Arya Samaj was founded by Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 AD. This society functioned as a Hindu reform movement. People who believed in Arya Samaj believed in pure Vedic tradition and opposed superstitions like idol worship, sacrifice etc.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was to receive first 'Bharat Ratna'?
Explanation: Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian honor of the country which was started in 1954 AD. The first person from India to be honored with Bharat Ratna was Dr. S Radhakrishnan. He was the first Vice President and second President of India. His birthday, 5th September, is celebrated every year as Teacher's Day.
Subject: Art & Culture

Questions: Who was the second Muslim President of the Indian National Congress?
Explanation: The Indian National Congress was established on 28 December 1885 AD. Its first president was W.C. Banerjee. The first Muslim President of Congress was Badruddin Tyabji who presided over the Madras session of 1887. The second Muslim President of the Congress was Rahimtullah Sayani who presided over the 1896 session. Under his chairmanship, 'Vande Mataram' was sung for the first time in 1896. The first woman president of Congress was Annie Besant while the first Indian woman president was Sarojini Naidu.

Option B: Gopalkrishna Gokhale and Rash Behari Bose

Explanation:

The Ryotwari system was started in 1820 AD by the then Governor of Madras, Thomas Munro, which was implemented in Madras, Bombay and Assam. The Bombay Plan was proposed by a group of famou industrialists of India, which included JRD Tata Ghanshyam Das Birla, John Mathai etc. This plan was also known as Birla-Tata Plan. The main points of thi scheme were as follows –

• This plan accepted a planned economy.
• It proposed a scheme without foreign capital investment.
• It played an important role in the state economy

64th BPSC
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: There was a proposal in the Bombay Plan.

Questions: Who began the 'Faraizi Movement'?
Explanation: The main objective of the Faraizi movement was to bring reform in the religion of Islam. The area of influence of this movement was in East Bengal. Thi movement was started by Haji Shariatullah in 1818 AD
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who wrote the book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’?
Explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was an Indian Parsi intellectual educationist and social politician. He is known as the 'Grand Old Man' of India. The book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’ written by him had drawn the attention of Indians towards the drain of money from India in Britain
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Who wrote the book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’?

Questions: Who raised the flag of Independence at the Congress Session of 1929?
Explanation: In the year 1929, ‘Complete Swaraj’ was announced in the Lahore session of Congress. This session was presided over by Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru. Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the Indian flag on the banks of river Ravi on 31 December 1929. Jawahar Lal Nehru is considered a staunch supporter of socialism. In this convention, it was announced to celebrate the first Independence Day on 26 January 1930.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Who raised the flag of Independence at the Congress Session of 1929?

Questions: Which of the following was not the reason for making the sepoys of the East India Company rebellious?
Option A: The efforts of the officers of the Company to spread Christianity
Option B: The order to the sepoys to travel on ships
Explanation: The reasons for the rebellion of 1857 AD were not the incompetence of the East India Company officials, but their religious political policies and discrimination against Indians were the main reasons. The immediate cause was the trigger of the Enfield rifle which used pig and cow fat in its cartridges. Due to which both Hindu and Muslim communities were hurt.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Which of the following was not the reason for making the sepoys of the East India Company rebellious?

Questions: About Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar, it was sais that his empire extended form
Explanation:
It is said about Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar that the extent of his rule was from 'Chandni Chowk to Palam'. After the rebellion of 1857 AD, Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to Rangoon.

Note – The question has been deleted as disputed by the Commission.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: About Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar, it was sais that his empire extended form

Questions: Who among the following did not rebel against the British East India Company’s control over them?
Explanation: The Nizam of Hyderabad did not protest against the control of the English Company. The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 AD and this empire ended before the rule of the East India Company. Apart from this, the rebellion of Dewan Veluthampi of Travancore lasted till 1808-1809 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The immediate cause of the 'Deccan Riots' of 1875 was
Option B: High interest rates charged by Mahajan
Option D: Protect against imposition of religious reforms
Answer: (B) (B) High interest rates charged by Mahajans
Explanation: The immediate cause of the riots in the Deccan was the high interest rates charged by moneylenders. The area of influence of the Deccan Revolt was the Western Ghats. This rebellion started in 1875 AD. The Deccan Revolt is related to the state of Maharashtra.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Raini Palme Dutt said. "They both fought and collaborated with imperialism." Which political grouping was he referring to?
Explanation: The Indian National Congress was established on 28 December 1885 AD and it continued to adopt liberal policy till 1905 AD. After 1905 AD, it made some changes in its policies which have been criticized by Rajni Pam Dutt. According to him, Congress both fought and cooperated with imperialism.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following was not a 'nationalist' newspaper?
Explanation: ‘Times of India’ was an English language daily newspaper and was not a nationalist magazine. Whereas The Hindu, Bengali etc. were nationalist magazines.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: Identify the correct combination from the options given below for Prarthana Samaj, Young India, Lokhitwadi, Satyashodhak Samaj, Rahnumai Mazdayasan Sabha :

Option B: Atmaram Pandurang, Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, Gopal Hari Deshmukh, Jyotiba Phule, Naoroji Furdonji

Questions: Bal Gangadhar Tilak came to be known as 'Lokmanya Tilak', when-
Option C: The government accused him in the Rand Murder Case
Option D: He started Shivaji and Ganpati festival
Answer: (C) (C) The government accused him in the Rand Murder Case
Explanation:
In the year 1897 AD, Bal Gangadhar Tilak was given the title of 'Lokmanya'. This title was given during the tria that followed the Rand Amherst murder. Tilak remained in jail for 18 months in connection with thi case.

Note – The answer given by the Commission is (E).
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: The Hindu, Kesari, Bengalee, Hindustani, Sudharak

Questions: How old was Bhagat Singh when he threw a bomb in the assembly in protest against the government?
Explanation: Bhagat Singh was born in September 1907 AD and he threw a bomb in the Central Assembly in April 1929 AD against the Public Safety Bill. After this Bhagat Singh was arrested. When Bhagat Singh threw the bomb, he was a little more than 21 years old.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre happened in the context of which Gandhian Satyagraha?
Explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh incident took place on 13 April 1919. A meeting was organized in Jallianwala Bagh, Punjab to protest against the Rowlatt Act. On the instructions of General Dyer, bullets were fired at this meeting in which more than 900 people were killed.
Subject: History of India

Questions: At which territory did tribals rebel against the British?
Explanation:
In Bihar (present-day Jharkhand), the tribals revolted against the British under the leadership of Birsa Munda. This rebellion is also known as ‘Ulgulan rebellion. This rebellion was the first strong tribal rebellion against the British. Apart from this, tribal rebellions also took place in Bengal, Assam, Maharashtra etc.

Note – Option (E) has been considered correct by the Commission.
Subject: Geography

Questions: “So always with the assent and often to the dictates of the Chamber of commerce, the Government of India is carried on, and this is the ‘White Man’s Burden’.” Who said this?
Explanation: The above statement was given by Sachchidanand Sinha in the context of Lord Curzon. Sachchidanand Sinha was the first temporary President of the Constituent Assembly. He had a major contribution in establishing the state of Bihar as a separate state from Bengal.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following was the first Satyagraha of Mahatma Gandhi in India?
Explanation: The first Satyagraha was carried out by Mahatma Gandhi in Champaran in India in the year 1917. His movement proved to be a milestone in the Indian freedom struggle. This movement was done in protest against the Teenkathiya system forcibly imposed on the farmers in Champaran. Mahatma Gandhi was directly involved in Indian politics through the Champaran Satyagraha for the first time.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Gandhiji's Non-Cooperation Movement, urged people to avoid alcohol. This resulted in a serious loss of revenue for the government. The government of a province circulated a list of prominent individuals who drank alcohol as a device to persuade people to start drinking again. Name the province.
Explanation: The non-cooperation movement in India started in 1920 AD. In this movement, Gandhiji urged people to abstain from alcohol, which resulted in a huge reduction in British revenue. In order to reduce thi loss, the then government of Bihar had again encouraged people to consume alcohol
Subject: History of India

Questions: The elected Government of Bihar resigned in February 1938 for which reason?
Option A: The participation of India in war
Option B: Satyagraha against the British at the call of Gandhi
Option C: High taxes being imposed by the British
Option D: For the Release of political prisoners
Answer: (D) (D) For the Release of political prisoners
Explanation:
The elected government of Bihar resigned in 1938 in protest against not releasing political prisoners. This government was formed under the Government of India Act 1935 in the elections held in 1937.

63rd BPSC
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Which of the following princely states was not annexed by the British?
Explanation: The British did not include the Gwalior state in their territory. Sindh was included in the British territory by the British in 1843, Awadh in 1854. Under Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse, Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1849), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854) were included in the British territory.
Subject: Geography

Questions: What was the ultimate goal of Gandhiji’s Salt Satyagraha?
Option C: Economic relief to the common people
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: Salt Satyagraha was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930 to repeal the salt laws. This Satyagraha was a historic step in the Indian freedom struggle. The only objective of Gandhiji's Salt Satyagraha was to repeal the Salt Law and provide economic relief to the common people. More than one option is correct.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The Moplah Rebellion of 1921 broke out in
Explanation: The Moplah rebellion took place in Kerala in the year 1921. This rebellion was led by Ali Musaliar. The main reason for this rebellion was the high tax rates being collected from the farmers, but later this rebellion expanded due to communal reasons.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: The Swadeshi Movement took place in India during
Option C: The protest against the Rowlatt Act
Explanation: The partition of Bengal was announced by Lord Curzon on 19 July 1905, in protest against which the Swadesh movement was started. This movement was led by Haider Raza in Delhi and Chidambaram Pillai in Madras. The partition of Bengal was canceled by Lord Hardinge II in 1911 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Whom did Rajendra Prasad considered as the father of Pakistan?
Explanation: Separate electorate and separate constituencies for Muslims were established by the Morley-Minto Act (1909). Lord Minto was the Viceroy of India in 1909 AD. Due to these activities of Lord Minto, Rajendra Prasad considered him the father of Pakistan.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Bombay Presidency Association was established by
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: Bombay Presidency Association was established in 188 AD. It was founded by Firozshah Mehta, Tyabjee, K. T Tailang did it. This organization was started to help Indians receive western education and adopt thei culture to uplift India. An English newspaper 'The Bombay Chronicle' was also started by Firozshah Mehta.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Who established Imperial Cadet Corps?
Explanation: The Imperial Cadet Corps was established by Lord Curzon in November 1904. Under this, cadet related education was given to the youth of 17 to 20 years of age.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was given life punishment for the murder of Colonel Wyllie?
Explanation: Madanlal Dhingra was given death sentence for the murder of Colonel Wylie. Colonel Wylie was a retired officer of the Indian Army. Who lived in London. Madanlal Dhingra was hanged in Paintville Jail on 17 August 1909 on charges of murder.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: The post of the Indian High Commission was created by which Act?
Explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 is also known as the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms Act. Under this Act, the post of Indian High Commissioner was created. Under this Act, the system of diarchy was implemented in the provinces.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The Indian National Congress did not take part in which of the following Round Table Conferences?
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: The Indian National Congress did not participated in the first and third Round Table Conferences. Mahatma Gandhi participated in the Second Round Table Conference on behalf of Congress. The round table conferences which were held in 1930, 1931 and 1932 respectively, were attended by Muslim League and Bhimrao Ambedkar
Subject: History of India

Questions: Mahatma Gandhi presided over which Session of the Indian National Congress?
Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belagavi session of the Indian National Congress in 1924. This is the only session which was presided over by Gandhiji, in thi session the Swaraj Party again merged with the Congress.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was not the member of the Cabinet Mission?
Explanation: The Cabinet Mission reached India in the year 1946 AD. The main objective of this mission was to convince Indian leaders that the government was ready to compromise on constitutional matters. This mission was headed by Pethick Lawrence and its other members were Stafford Cripps and A. Was V.Alexander.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who wrote the pamphlet 'Now or Never'?
Explanation: Now and Never pamphlet was written by Chaudhary Rahmat Ali. Through this pamphlet, Chaudhary Rahmat Ali demanded a separate country Pakistan and he gave the slogan ‘If not now, then never’. This pamphlet was first published in 1933 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who declared 'Sati' illegal?
Explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy made a lot of efforts to eradicate the practice of Sati in India, as a result of which this movement gained strength and the then British government was forced to make a law to stop the practice of Sati. The credit for declaring the practice of Sati completely illegal in India goes to Lord William Bentinck. This practice was declared illegal by Regulation XVII in 1829 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: When was the Punjab Land Alienation Act passed?
Explanation: The Punjab Land alienation Act was passed in 1900. By passing this Act, Curzon saved the farmers of Punjab from eviction by moneylenders. Under this Act, cooperative societies and agricultural banks were established for the convenience of farmers.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The Department of State was established under whose leadership?
Explanation:
The Department of State was established in 1947 under the chairmanship of Sardar Patel. The main objective of this department was to promote the political integration of India by securing the accession of the princely states into India.

60th -62nd BPSC
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: ' The Muslims, if contented and satisfied would become the greatest bulwark of British power in India.” Who wrote it?
Explanation: In the book ‘The Indian Muslim’ written by Sir William Wilson Hunter, it has been said that ‘If the Muslims are happy and satisfied, then the British power in India will continue to be protected. After this statement of Hunter, there was a change in the attitude of the British government towards the Muslim community.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who was the leader of the revolutionaries in Bihar during the revole of 1857?
Explanation: Babu Veer Kunwar Singh, the royal landlord of Jagdishpur (Ara), had led the revolutionary activities in Bihar during the rebellion of 1857 AD. Veer Kunwar Singh was adept in the art of guerrilla warfare. Even at the age of 80, he fiercely faced the British rule.
Subject: History of Bihar
Subtopic: Leaders of the revolt in Bihar

Questions: Who was elected the first president of All India Kisan Sabha in Lucknow in 1936?
Explanation: All India Kisan Sabha was formed on 11 April 1936. Its first president and secretary were Swami Sahajanand Saraswati and N.G. Ranga respectively. The All India Kisan Sabha issued a Peasant Manifesto in August 1936 in which they demanded the abolition of the Zamindari system and the abolition of debts of rural farmers.
Subject: History of Bihar
Subtopic: First President of All India Kisan Sabha

Questions: 'In my belief, Congress is to tottering to its fall and one of my great ambitions while in India is to assist it to a peaceful demise.” Who wrote it?
Explanation: The tenure of Lord Curzon was till (1899-1905) and during his reign British imperialism was at its peak. In the year 1900, he had said that in my belief, congress is to tottering to Its fall and one of my great ambitions while in India is to assist it to a peaceful demise.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Sir Michael O’Dwyer was shot dead on 13<sup>th</sup> March, 1940 in London by :
Explanation: Sir Michael O'Dwyer was the main culprit of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. He held the post of Lieutenant Governor in Punjab from 1912 to 1919 AD. Udham Singh shot dead Michael O'Dwyer in London on 13 March 1940. Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919. Hurt by this incident, Mahatma Gandhi returned the title of 'Kaiser-e-Hind'.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the Prime Minister of England when the Montague-Chelmsford Act was passed in 1919?
Explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 is also known as the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms Act. When this Act was passed in December 1919, the Prime Minister of England was Lloyd George.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Prime Minister of England during Montague-Chelmsford Act

Questions: Who is regarded as " the Mother of Indian Revolution"?
Explanation: Madam Bhikhaji Rustom Cama has been called the “Mother of the Indian Revolution”. He prepared the outline of Indian independence in Britain, America and Germany and on 22 August 1907, he first hoisted the Indian flag in Stuttgart, Germany.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who became champion of socialism and wanted overthrow of British rule, Princely states, landlordism and capitalism in 1933?
Explanation: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru is considered a staunch supporter of socialism. He not only appealed for the overthrow of British rule but also called for the abolition of princely states, zamindari system and capitalism. Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Indian National Congress session three times, in 1929, 1936 and 1937 respectively.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The Chittagong Armoury Raid had been planned by :
Explanation: On 18 April 1930, the attack on Chittagong armory was carried out under the leadership of Surya Sen. About 65 members of the Hindustan Republican Army were involved in this raid. The Chittagong site is currently located in Bangladesh.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which journal was not associated with the revolutionary activities?
Explanation: In the year 1919, a weekly magazine named Young India was published by Mahatma Gandhi. Through this magazine, Gandhiji used to publish things related to the propagation of his ideology and the use of nonviolence in the movements to be organized. The main objective of publishing the book Yantra India was to emphasize on non-violent activities.
Subject: History of India

Questions: First Indian elected to the British House of Commons, was Dadabhai Naoroji who contested on the ticket of :
Explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was the first Indian to be elected to the “British House of Commons” in 1892 AD. He had contested this election on the ticket of Liberal Party Dadabhai Naoroji had presided over the sessions of the Indian National Congress in 1886 AD and 1906 AD. He is called the father of Indian politics.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Swaraj Party was formed following the failure of:
Explanation: Swaraj Party was established on 1 January 1923 with the efforts of Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru. This party was established after the failure of the non-cooperation movement, whose main objective was to work for the attainment of political independence and self-rule
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who organized the 'Khudai Khidmatgar' in 1929?
Explanation: Khudai Khidmatgar was established in 1929 AD by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan. Khudai Khidmatgar means “Servant of God”. It was a movement against the British government by the Pathans in the North-Western Provinces under the leadership of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, also known as the 'Red shirts' movement. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan is also known as frontier Gandhi.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The Cabinet Mission came to India-
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: The Cabinet Mission reached India on 24 March 1946. There were three members of this mission which are as follows – Pethick Lawrence (President), Sir Stafford Cripps, A. V.Alexander. The main objective of the Cabinet Mission's arrival in India was to provide independence to India as well as to transfer power from the British government to the Indian leadership.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The precursor of Indian National Congress was :
Explanation: The Indian Association was founded by Anand Mohan Bose and Surendranath Banerjee in 1876 AD. This organization was a nationalist organization which was later merged into the Indian National Congress.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who is known as father of Dyarchy?
Explanation: British officer Sir Leonil Cartis is called the father of diarchy in India. In the year 1915, he first suggested this system which was later named Diarchy.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Akhil Bhartiya Kisan Congress was founded in :
Explanation: All India Kisan Sabha was established in 1936 AD. In the Congress session of 1936, Jawahar Lal Nehru made Swami Sahajanand Saraswati its first president. It was established in Lucknow.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which among the following year Surendra Nath Bannerjee was eliminated form Indian Civil Services?
Explanation: Surendranath Banerjee had succeeded in the Indian Civil Service Examination in the year 1869 and was appointed to serve in Sylhet (Assam). Due to some mistake, the British Government expelled him from service in 1874 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which among the following viceroy period the title of ‘Rai Bahadur’ and ‘Khan Bahadur’ were began to conferred to Indian ?
Explanation:
Lord Lytton's tenure was till (1876-80). He was the first to start the practice of conferring the titles of Khan Bahadur and Rai Bahadur. It was during his reign that Queen Victoria was declared the Empress of India.

56th -59th BPSC
Subject: History of India

Questions: In which year was the 'Regulating Act' passed?
Explanation: The Regulating Act was passed in 1773 AD. Its main objective was to check the rule of the East India Company in India. In place of this Act, Pitt's India Act was implemented in 1784 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the Governor General of India in 1857?
Explanation: Lord Canning's tenure was till (1856-1862) and the revolution of 1857 took place during his reign. During his reign, the British Government ended the rule of the East India Company under the Government of India Act 1858. Canning was the first Viceroy of India.
Subject: History of India

Questions: After which incident Mahatma Gandhi had called Non-Cooperation Movement as his ‘Himalayan Blunder’?
Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi had started the non-cooperation movement on 1 August 1920, but after the Chauri-Chaura incident that occurred on 5 February 1922, he decided to withdraw the non-cooperation movement on 11 February 1922.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which movement started after partition of Bengal?
Explanation: The partition of Bengal was announced by Lord Curzon on 16 July 1905. In protest against this, the Swadeshi movement was started on 7 August 1905. The objective of this movement was to boycott British goods and to emphasize on using more Indian goods.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the first Indian woman president of the Indian National Congress?
Explanation: The Indian National Congress was established on 28 December 1885 AD. The first woman president of the Indian National Congress was Annie Besant. She was elected as president in the Calcutta session of year 1917. She presided over the Calcutta session this year. The first Indian woman president was Sarojini Naidu, who became the president in the Kanpur session of 1925.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Where did Madam Cama hoist the first tricolour flag in 1907?
Explanation: On 22 August 1907, the Indian flag was hoisted by Madam Cama in Stuttgart, Germany. This incident i also called ‘Berlin Committee Flag’.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who founded the Pagal Panthi?
Explanation: Panth was founded by Karamshah. , Pagal Panthi wa a religious sect which had influence in Bengal. In 1825 AD, Karamshah and Tipu rebelled against the landlords and in 1833 AD the British suppressed this rebellion.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who were the Faraizis?
Explanation: Faraizi were a followers of Haji Shariatullah. The Faraji movement was started in 1818 AD and its area of expansion was Bengal. The main objective of this movement was to bring reform in the religion of Islam.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The correct geographical location for the Ramosi Uprising was
Explanation: The people of Ramosi caste living in the Western Ghats revolted under the leadership of 'Chittur Singh' in 1822 AD. This rebellion continued continuously from 1822 – 1839. The main reason for this rebellion was the problem of famine and hunger.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The Waghera Uprising happened in
Explanation: The Waghera rebellion was fought against the British government in 1818 AD. The Wagheras of Okha-mandal opposed the British rule from the beginning. This rebellion lasted from 1818 to 1820 AD.
Subject: Geography

Questions: In order to control the media in India, ‘Acts’ were passed in
Explanation:
Some acts were made to control the press in India, which are as follows.

• Press Act – 1835
• Licensing Act – 1867
• Vernacular Press Act – 1878
• The Newspaper Act - 1908
Subject: Geography

Questions: The process of split in the Congress in the early years of the twentieth century began over
Option C: Participation of the people in the Congress movement
Explanation: The Indian National Congress was established in 1885 AD. Congress has an important contribution in India's independence, but the process of division also took place from time to time, the main reason for which was that in the initial years, Congress was dominated by liberals. The liberals had adopted the legal path to achieve their goal. In many cases there were differences of opinion regarding objectives and public participation.
Subject: History of India

Questions: 'New Lamps for Old' was a series of articles (1893- 94) that criticized the Congress for being out of touch with the 'proletariat'. Who was the author of these articles?
Explanation: Aurobindo Ghosh was a prominent leader of revolutionary movements in Bengal. He had published Yugantar, Karmayogi, Dharma etc. ‘The Life Divine’ is one of his major books. He established Pondicherry Ashram in 1910 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Fill in the blanks: The Nehru Report was drafted by a committee headed by ________ and the subject was _
Option A: Motilal Nehru and Jawaharlal Nehru; India's relationship with the British Empire
Option B: Jawaharlal Nehru; local Self-Government in india
Option C: Motilal Nehru; Constitutional arrangements in India
Option D: Jawaharlal Nehru; Constitutional arrangements in India
Answer: (C) (C) Motilal Nehru; Constitutiona arrangements in India
Explanation: The Nehru Report was published under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru in 1928 AD. In this the basic goals for the future Indian Constitution were laid down. Besides, the proposal of “Dominion State” for India was also made.
Subject: History of India

Questions: What was the common relationship between Katherine Mayo, Aldous Huxley, Charles Andrews and William Digby?
Option A: They wrote commentaries on the condition of India during British rule
Option B: They were supporters of Indian National Movement
Option C: They were opponents of the Indian national Movement
Option D: They were friends of Mahatma Gandh
Answer: (A) (A) He wrote comments on the condition of India during the British rule.
Explanation:
In the year 1924, the book 'Mother India' was written by Katherine Mayo in which deep commentary wa made on Indian society, culture and religion

▪ Charles Andrews was an associate of Mahatma Gandhi and wrote several books and commentaries during the Indian independence struggle

▪ Aldous Huxley also wrote on the condition of Indian society during the independence movement. Suggestions for independence are given in his work 'Eclipse of Baranasi'.
▪ William Digby advocated complete economic, racial equality, representative government, and self-government.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who penned the following lines? “Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil me hai/Dekhna hai zor kitna baju-e-qatil me hai”.
Explanation: Revolutionary Ramprasad Bismil had written ‘Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil mein hai’ in Urdu language. Ram Prasad Bismil was also a member of the Hindustan Republican Association and was hanged at the age of 30 in the Kakori conspiracy case. Note - In the subsequent examination, BPSC did not consider Bismil as its author. Its creator is Bismil Azimabadi.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who raised the demand for 'Complete Independence' for the first time in 1921?
Explanation: The demand for complete independence was first made by Hasrat Mohani in the year 1921 and it was he who first wrote the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' with his pen. Later this slogan was popularized by Bhagat Singh. Hasrat Mohani was in favor of Hindu Muslim unity.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Identify the nearest years those are closest to the founding of the Communist Party of India and the RSS respectively.
Explanation: The Communist Party of India was established in 1925 AD and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh was established in Nagpur in 1925 by K. It was done by D. Hedgewar.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati formed the All India United Kisan Sabha with the demand for the ‘nationalization of land and waterways’.
Option A: Just before his death(B) At a very young age
Explanation: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati had formed the All India Kisan Sabha in the year 1936. He took many steps to solve the problems of farmers. It was he who formed the Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which Round Table Conference held in 1932?
Explanation:
The three Round Table Conferences were organized in 1930, 1931 and 1932 respectively. Mahatma Gandhi participated in the second Round Table Conference on behalf of Congress. In the Third Round Table Conference in 1932, a white paper was issued which later became the basis of the Government of India Act 1935.

53rd -55th BPSC
Subject: History of India

Questions: "Swaraj is my birthright, I shall have it." Who said?
Explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born in 1856 AD. He was a nationalist leader, social reformer and freedom fighter He gave the slogan “Swaraj is our birthright”. Ba Gangadhar Tilak is also known as Lokmanya. He ha been called the father of 'Indian unrest' by the British colonial authority.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Madras Mahajan Sabha was established in
Explanation: Madras Mahajan Sabha was founded by Ramaswam Mudaliar in 1884 AD. The purpose of its establishment was to coordinate the work of the local organization.
Subject: History of India

Questions: How many delegates participated in the first session of the Indian National Congress?
Explanation: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held on 28 December 1885, which continued till 31 December 1885. A total of 72 delegates participated in it. W.C. Banerjee presided over this session. This convention was held in Bombay.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Number of delegates in first session of Indian National Congress

Questions: The first Indian Governor General of independent India was –
Explanation: The first Indian Governor General of independent India was C. Rajagopalachari. He is also known as the last Governor General of India. He was awarded Bharat Ratna in 1954 AD. C. Rajagopalachari was also called Chanakya of Indian politics.
Subject: History of India

Questions: When was the National Council of Education established?
Explanation: The National Council of Education was established on 15 August 1906. The objective of which was to spread science and technology to promote indigenous industrial revolution.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Non-cooperation movement was started in the year
Explanation: The non-cooperation movement was started on 1 August 1920 in protest against the Khilafat movement and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. This movement had to be postponed after the Chauri-Chaura incident in 1922. Mahatma Gandhi had described the noncooperation movement as a mistake like the Himalayan Blunder.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Montagu-Chelmsford Report -
Option A: Formed the basis of the Indian Independence Act, 1947
Option B: Formed the basis of the Indian Council Act, 1909
Option C: Formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919
Option D: Formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1935.
Answer: (C) (C) Formed the basis of the Governmen of India Act, 1919
Explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 was made on the basis of Montague-Chelmsford report. It was through this Act that the system of dual governance wa implemented in the provinces.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who among these was famous as 'Sher-e-Punjab'?
Explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai, a native of Punjab state, is known as Sher-e-Punjab. In the year 1920, he presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress, in which Gandhiji presented the proposal of noncooperation movement. He gave the slogan “ Simon Go back” in protest against Simon Commission.
Subject: History of India

Questions: When was Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
Explanation: An agreement was reached between Mahatma Gandh and Irwin on 5 March 1931, which is known as the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. This agreement is also known a Delhi Agreement. After this agreement, Indians were given the right to make salt on the sea shore for domestic use.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which of the following Round Table Conference was held in 1932?
Explanation: The Third Round Table Conference was organized from 17 November to 24 December 1932. Congress did not participate in this conference. It was in the Third Round Table Conference that the “Government of India Act 1935” was finalized
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who is related to 'Abhinav Bharat'?
Explanation: Abhinav Bharat was founded by V.D. Savarkar in 1904 AD. This was a revolutionary organization. Mitra Mela organization was established in the year 1899 and in 1904 AD it was merged into Abhinav Bharat. He established “Abhinav Bharat Society” in London in 1906.
Subject: History of India

Questions: 'Do or Die' is related to which movement?
Explanation: Quit India Movement was started by Mahatma Gandh on 8 August 1942. The Quit India Movement was proposed by Jawahar Lal Nehru which was supported by Sardar Patel. The slogan of “Do or Die” was given during the Quit India Movement.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the founder of 'Prarthana Samaj'?
Explanation: Prarthana Samaj was established in 1867 AD by Atmaram Pandurang. This society was established for religious and social reforms during the Indian Renaissance. The main objective of establishing this society was to worship God through prayer and service.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the father of Indian Renaissance Movement?
Explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy is considered the father of Indian Renaissance. He has a special contribution in the field of social and religious renaissance. He founded Brahmo Samaj in 1828 AD. He has made an important contribution in eradicating the practice of Sati from India. He published magazines like Samvad Kaumudi, Mirat-ul-Akhbar.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who founded 'Swaraj Dal'?
Explanation: Swaraj Party was founded on 1 January 1923 by Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das. The main objective of this party was to achieve self-rule and political independence for Indians.
Subject: History of India

Questions: 'Who founded the Theosophical Society?
Explanation: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 by Madam H.P. Blavatsky. Its main objective was to encourage the study of various religions, philosophie and sciences. The motto of this society is “There is no religion better than truth”.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which of the following books was written by Tilak?
Explanation:
The author of the book Geeta Rahasya is Bal Gangadhar Tilak. It was Tilak who started the Ganpati festival. In 1881 AD, he published a magazine named Kesari in Marathi language. Tilak is also called “the father of Indian unrest.” Tilak died on 1 August 1920 in Bombay.

Book
Author
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Congress passed the 'Swaraj' resolution in the year 1905. The purpose of the proposal was -
Option A: Right to make constitution for oneself, but it did not happen
Explanation: Congress had passed the Swaraj Resolution in the year 1905, the objective of which was to ensure self-rule. The Congress session held in 1905 was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: Provincial governments were formed under which of the following Acts?
Explanation:
The formation of provincial governments was proposed in the Act of 1935. By this Act, a federal government was established in India and the system of dyarchy was introduced at the Centre. By this act Burma was separated from India.

48th -52nd BPSC
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Where did the Moplah rebellion of 1921 take place?
Explanation: The Moplah rebellion was carried out in 1921 AD by the Moplah Muslims in Kerala against the Hindu landlords. In this rebellion, an attempt was made by the British to create riots between Hindus and Muslims. The novel named Mopla was written by V.D. Savarkar.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: When did Queen Victoria announce the taking over of the Indian administration under the control of the British Crown?
Explanation: On 1 November 1858, Lord Canning read the proclamation of Queen Victoria in the Durbar held at Minto Park, Allahabad. According to which the Company's rule in India was ended and handed over directly to the British Crown.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Match Up (a) Bardoli (1) Maharashtra (b) Chauri Chaura (2) Gujarat (c) Yervada (3) West Bengal (d) Noakhali (4) Uttar Pradesh code : a b c d
Explanation: Option (C) of the above question is correctly matched A place named Bardoli is situated in Gujarat, Chauri Chaura place in Uttar Pradesh, Yerwada Jail in Maharashtra and Noakhali in West Bengal.
Subject: History of India

Questions: In which year did Lord Curzon cancel the partition of Bengal?
Explanation: The partition of Bengal was announced by Lord Curzon on 19 July 1905. Which came into effect from 16 October 1905 AD. Due to this partition, mourning day wa observed throughout Bengal. The partition of Benga was canceled by Viceroy Harding in 1911 AD.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: When did the British Government appoint the Saddler University Commission for the reform of education?
Explanation: Sadler Commission was formed in 1917, Under the leadership of Michael E Sandler. This commission was formed for educational reforms. It gave many important instructions in its suggestions, after which vast improvements were seen in the education sector. On the recommendation of this commission, “Board of Secondary Education” was established in Uttar Pradesh.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: During the reign of which British Governor was the first railway line laid in India?
Explanation: The first railway in India was operated on 16 April 1853 during the reign of Lord Dalhousie. The first train covered a distance of about 34 km, which ran between Mumbai and Thane. The second train in India was oprated between Howrah and Hooghly on 15 August 1854.
Subject: Geography

Questions: Why did Mahatma Gandhi support the Khilafat movement?
Option B: Gandhiji wanted to get the support of Indian Muslims in his movement against the British.
Option D: Khalifa was a good friend of Gandhiji
Answer: (B) (B) Gandhiji wanted to get the support of Indian Muslims in his movement against the British.
Explanation: The Khilafat movement was started in 1919 AD. This movement was started under the leadership of Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali. Mahatma Gandhi had given full support to this movement, because through this he wanted the cooperation of Indian Muslims in this fight for freedom.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: The method of movement of the moderate party leaders of Congress was:
Explanation: The method of movement of the moderate party leaders of the Congress was to carry out a royal-bound movement or to agitate within the ambit of the law. Their main objective was to develop the understanding of political awareness among Indians.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Why did people gather for demonstration in Jallianwala Bagh?
Option A: To protest against the arrest of Gandhiji and Lajpat Rai
Option B: To protest against the arrest of Kitchlu and Satyapal
Option D: To protest against the inhuman activities of the Punjab Government
Answer: (B) (B) To protest against the arrest of Kitchlu and Satyapal.
Explanation: People had gathered at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar on 13 April 1919 to protest against the arrest of Dr. Satyapal and Dr. Kitchlu. All these people were peacefully protesting against his arrest, but General Dyer opened fire on all these present people in which about 5 thousand people were killed and many people were injured.
Subject: History of India

Questions: With whose inspiration did the women's movement start in India?
Explanation:
Jyotiba Phule had established a girls' school in Pune in 1898 AD for girls' education. Satyashodhak Samaj was established by him in 1873 AD. The women's movement in India was started with their efforts.

• The author of the book Gulamgiri is Jyotiba Phule
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the first Indian to protest against political reforms?
Explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was the first to raise his voice for political reforms. East India Association was established by him in 1867. Naoroji was the first Asian person to become a member of Britain's “House of Commons”.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Before the establishment of Indian Nationa Congress, the most important organization was:
Explanation: The Indian National Congress was established on 28 December 1885 AD. The most prominent among the predecessor institutions of the Congress was the East India Association, which was established in 1867 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The founder of Forward Bloc was-
Explanation: After the Tripuri session of the Congress, Subhash Chandra Bose had established the Forward Bloc within the Congress in 1939 with the aim of making the Congress a symbol of democracy and revolution. Subhash Chandra Bose is also known as Netaji.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the first President of Indian Trade Union Congress?
Option C: Lala Lajpat Rai (D) N. M. Joshi
Explanation: The first president of All India Trade Union was Lala Lajpat Rai. This union was established in 1920 AD. It was formed with the aim of representing India in the International Labor Organization.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: First President of Indian Trade Union Congress

Questions: Where was the All India Kisan Mahasabha organized for the first time?
Explanation: All India Kisan Sabha was established in 1936 AD. Its first meeting was held in Lucknow. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati became its first president and N.G. Ranga was made its secretary.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Location of All India Kisan Mahasabha's first organization

Questions: Under whose leadership did the rebellion of 1857 take place in Lucknow?
Explanation: The revolution of 1857 in Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal. She was the wife of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Awadh. The revolution of 1857 was led by various great personalities in different cities of India, including Kunwar Singh in Bihar and Rani Lakshmi Bai in Jhansi.
Subject: History of India

Questions: When was the Rowlatt Act passed?
Explanation: Rowlatt Act is also known as Black Law. This law was passed on 18 March 1919. Under this Act, the government was given powers to suppress political activities and was allowed to detain political prisoners without trial for two years. This Act was passed during the reign of Lord Chelmsford (1916-21)
Subject: History of India

Questions: When did Gandhiji start the non-cooperation movement?
Explanation: The non-cooperation movement was started on 1 August 1920 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. After the Chauri-Chaura incident, Mahatma Gandhi had decided to withdraw this movement on 12 February 1922.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Start date of the non-cooperation movement

Questions: When did the Quit India Movement started?
Explanation: On 8 August 1942, the resolution for Quit India Movement was passed in the Congress session at Gwalia Tank Ground in Bombay. After which, on 9 August 1942, this movement was started all over India. Gandhiji had given the slogan of “Do or Die” in this movement.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Start date of the Quit India Movement

Questions: After the rebellion of 1857, the British government selected the soldiers-
Option A: Among the Brahmins of UP and Bihar.
Option B: Of the Bengali and Oriya people of the East.
Option C: Among the Gorkhas, Sikhs and Punjabis of the North.
Answer: (C) (C) Among the Gorkhas, Sikhs and Punjabis of the North.
Explanation: After the Revolution of 1857, the British government had decided to recruit Gorkha soldiers from Uttar Pradesh and Sikh soldiers from Punjab.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Start date of the Quit India Movement

Questions: The revolutionary phase of trade unions in India was-
Explanation:
The revolutionary phase of trade unions in India started from 1926 – 1939 AD. The All India Trade Union was established in 1920, which was the first organized organization related to workers. Its first president was Lala Lajpat Rai.

48th BPSC
Subject: History of India

Questions: Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Rammohan Roy in?
Explanation: Brahmo Samaj was established by Raja Rammohan Roy in the year 1828 AD. Brahmo Samaj was a socioreligious organization of India. Under Brahmo Samaj, many religious traditions like Sati, child marriage etc. were abolished. Raja Ram Mohan Roy is considered the father of Indian Renaissance.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: 'Satyarth Prakash' was composed by
Explanation: Satyarth Prakash was written by Swami Dayanand Saraswati. The main objective of writing Satyarth Prakash was to propagate the principles of Arya Samaj. There are total 14 chapters in this book. Dayanand Saraswati first used the word Swarajya (Swadesh) in this.
Subject: Art & Culture

Questions: ‘Anushilan Samiti’ was-
Option C: Interested in the welfare of workers
Explanation: Anushilan Samiti was an anti-British secret revolutionary organization formed in Bengal during India's freedom struggle during the colonial period. It was established together in 1907 AD by Varindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendra Dutt. The objective of this committee was to follow the path shown by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The policy of 'Ring fence' is related to-
Explanation: The policy of the security cell/Ring fence was related to Warren Hastings. The objective of this policy was to protect the company's boundaries by creating buffe zones. The states included in this policy were assured of providing military assistance against external aggression at their own expenses.
Subject: History of India

Questions: 'Who was the first president of All India Trade Union Congress?
Explanation: All India Trade Union Congress was established in 1920 AD. Whose first president was Lala Lajpat Rai. The main objective of its establishment was to solve the problems of labor unions and to represent India in the International Labor Organization.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: The Prime Minister of England at the time of Quit India Movement was –
Explanation: Quit India Movement was started on 8 August 1942. At this time the Prime Minister of England was Winston Churchill. His tenure was from 1940 – 1945 AD. It was he who called Mahatma Gandhi a “half-naked fakir"
Subject: History of India

Questions: Name the scholar of Deoband who played an important role in the freedom movement?
Explanation: The Deoband movement was a revivalist movement within Sunni Islam. In India, this movement took place mainly in Uttar Pradesh. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad belonged to the Deoband branch. After independence, Abul Kalam became the first education minister of the independent country.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Who was Shardamani?
Explanation: Shardamani was the wife of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. In Ramakrishna Sangh, she was known as “Shri Maa”. Shardamani was born in 1853 AD in Bengal. Shardamani was married to Ramakrishna Paramhamsa at the age of only 5 years. She died in the year 1920 AD. A grand temple has been built on his samadhi in Belur Math.
Subject: General Mental Ability & CSAT

Questions: When was it decided to include Enfield rifles fired with greased cartridges in the British Indian Army?
Explanation: It was decided by the British to include the Enfield rifle fired with greased cartridges in the Indian Army in December 1856. This cartridge became the immediate cause of the revolution of 1857. In this, the greased cartridge had to be bitten with the teeth and filled in the barrel of the rifle, which hurt the sentiments of Hindus and Muslims. The actual revolution of 1857 in India started from Meerut on 10 May 1857.
Subject: Internal Security

Questions: When was the All India Trade Union Congress established in Bombay?
Explanation: All India Trade Union Congress was established in 1920 AD. Whose first president was Lala Lajpat Rai. This organization was not only a friendly organization of businessmen but also of farmers. This organization believed that agriculture and trade complement each other.
Subject: Indian Economy
Subtopic: All India Trade Union Congress – Bombay

Questions: Who founded 'Amrit Bazaar Patrika'?
Explanation: Amrit Bazar Patrika is a leading Bengali language newspaper. It was established by Shishir Kumar Ghosh in 1868 AD. After the passing of the Vernacular Press Act, this magazine started being published in English also.
Subject: History of India
Subtopic: Lord Curzon – Founding of Amrit Bazaar Patrika

Questions: Who said that the Congress movement was neither inspired by the people, nor was it thought or planned by them?
Explanation: According to Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, the Congress movement was neither inspired by the people nor was it thought or planned by them. Ahmed Khan had established the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888 AD, whose main objective was to keep the policie of Congress away from the people and make them ineffective.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who played an important role in the signing of Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
Explanation: Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 AD. The contribution of Tej Bahadur Sapru in brokering a compromise between these two was commendable. Under this agreement, a political compromise was reached between Gandhi and Irwin, in which orders were given to release all the political prisoners except those accused of violence.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who propounded the theory of 'passive resistance'?
Explanation: The passive resistance theory was propounded by Aurobindo Ghosh in his book Bande Mataram Aurobindo Ghosh had applied this theory against the British, he believed that the British should be opposed fiercely until they leave India.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which of the following newspapers mainly promoted the policies of the liberals?
Explanation: Leader newspaper was published by Madan Mohan Malviya. This newspaper was a propagator of the policies of the liberals. The editor of Young India was Mahatma Gandhi while the editor of New India was Annie Besant.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the Congress President who held talks with both Cripps Mission and Lord Wavell?
Explanation: Cripps Mission came to India in 1942 AD. At this time, Abul Kalam was the President of the Indian National Congress. Lord Wavell also visited India in the year 1945. Hence, the person who talked to both Cripps Mission and Lord Wavell was Abul Kalam Azad. Abul Kalam Azad was the President of Congress from 1940- 1946 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: How many seats were given for the Dalit class in the Communal Award and Poona Pact respectively?
Explanation: On August 16 1932, the British PM Ramsay macdonald announced the communal award. Ponna pact was signed between Mahtama Gandhi and Ambedkar on 24 September 1932. According to this, the number of seats reserved for Harijans of the country was increased from 71 to 148.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who among the following industrialists was the treasurer of AICC for a long time and also went to jail in 1930?
Explanation: Jamnalal Bajaj was an Indian freedom fighter and businessman. He was the Treasurer of the Congress Committee from 1920 to 1942. He was a follower of Mahatma Gandhi. Jamnalal Bajaj was arrested during the freedom movement. He returned the title of Rai Bahadur given by the British. He died in Wardha in 1942 AD.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who was the leader of the Munda Revolution of 1899-1900?
Explanation: The father of Munda movement was Birsa Munda. This movement was the most powerful reaction against British colonial rule in the 19th century. This rebellion is also known as Ulgulan rebellion. Birsa Munda led this rebellion very actively. This rebellion extended to the areas of Jharkhand.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who presided over the first session of the All India Kisan Sabha?
Explanation:
All India Kisan Sabha was established in 1936 AD. Whose first president was Sahajanand Saraswati and secretary was N.G. Ranga. The purpose of establishing this assembly was to listen to the problems of the farmers and solve them. Sahajanand Saraswati wa born in 1889 AD and died in 1950 AD. He is called the father of the farmers movement in India.

CDPO (15.05.2022)
Subject: History of India

Questions: Where was the 'Ryotwari system' initially started?
Explanation: The Ryotwari system was introduced by Thomas Munro in 1820 AD in Madras and Bombay Presidencies Under this system the government entered into an agreement with the tenants for a fixed period.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The advocate who appeared for the INA trials at Delhi in 1945-46 was
Explanation: In 1945-46 AD, when the historic trial of INA started in the Red Fort of Delhi, Bhulabhai Desai was leading the defense. Tej Bahadur Sapru, K. Katju and Asaf Ali were among his assistants. On the first day of the proceedings, Jawaharlal Nehru was also present in the court after years, wearing a lawyer's attire.
Subject: Geography

Questions: Arrange the following events connected with Indian freedom struggle in the correct chronological order : 1. Muslim Deliverance Day 2. Direct Action Day 3. Resignation of Congress ministries 4. Individual Satyagraha Select the correct answer using the code given below.
Explanation:
• In October 1939, the Congress provincial government resigned due to political crises arising out of the Second World War. The Muslim League celebrated 22 December 1939 as 'Muslim Deliverance Day'.
• Individual Satyagraha is considered to have started from 17 October 1940 when Vinoba Bhave became its first Satyagrahi.
On 16 August 1946, the Muslim League advocated Direct Action Day and talked about taking Pakistan by violent means.
Subject: History of India

Questions: What is the chronological sequence of the following movements? 1. Deccan Riots 2. Indigo movement 3. Movement against land alienation in Punjab 4. Patni Movement Select the correct answer using the code given below.
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation:
• The Indigo Movement started in 1859 AD from Govindpur village in Nadia district of Bengal
• The Deccan riots started in 1875 AD.
• The Punjab Land Alienation Act was enacted in 1900 AD.
• Patni Movement
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: Who among the following leaders from Bihar appeared before the ‘Hammond Commission’ at Ranchi to demand voting rights for the Dalits?
Explanation: In 1935, Babu Jagjivan Ram appeared before the 'Hammond Commission' in Ranchi and demanded voting rights for Dalits for the first time.
Subject: Bihar Polity & Governance

Questions: Who among the following waged a rebellion against the British in Bihar immediately after the Battle of Buxar?
Explanation: After the battle of Buxar, when the Diwani of Bihar, Bengal and Orissa was handed over to the British in 1765 AD, then the officer of Hussepur Raj of Saran (presently located in Gopalganj district) demanded revenue from Maharaj Fateh Bahadur Shahi and the company Talked about accepting subordination. Maharaj Fateh Bahadur refused to accept both these things and rebelled and continued fighting guerilla wars for a long time.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Who among the following ‘Seven Martyrs’ of Patna during Quit India Movement was a student of B. N. College?
Explanation: Jagpati Kumar was a student of Bihar National College (B.N. College). He was born in 1923 AD in Kharant village of Obra block of Aurangabad district.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Who among the following were responsible for ‘Eka Movement’?
Answer: (A) (A) Farmers of Hardoi, Bahraich etc. in Awadh
Explanation: A movement was launched by the farmers of Hardoi, Bahraich and Sitapur etc. of Awadh against the exploitation of the landlords. This movement remained active during the non-cooperation movement.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Who among the following Viceroys was stabbed to death in Andaman Islands?
Explanation: Sher Ali Afridi, a Muslim Pathan, assassinated the Viceroy of India, Lord Mayo, in 1872 AD when he was reviewing the conditions and security arrangements of the prisoners of the Cellular Jail in Port Blair, Andaman Nicobar.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The Frontier Gandhi is known to have said that they have 'thrown to the wolves' him and his movement. Whom is he referring to?
Explanation: The Congress had a majority in the then Legislative Council of the North-West Frontier Province and had voted in favor of joining the Constituent Assembly, yet a referendum was imposed on that province on the question of choosing between India and Pakistan. The Congress boycotted the referendum in protest and the province acceded to Pakistan with a total of 50.99 percent votes (ie 9.52 percent of the total population of the province). Later, Frontier Gandhi (Abdul Ghaffar Khan) said with dismay that the Congress leadership had thrown him and his movement to the wolves.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Who did the Chief Khalsa Diwan declare as 'fallen' Sikhs and criminals?
Option C: The Leader of of the Nationalist Socialist Part
Explanation: The Chief Khalsa Diwan was involved in corruption and had the support of the British government. It issued orders declaring the Gadar agitators as fallen sikhs and criminals and declared Jallianwala Bagh murderer General Dyer a Sikh by presenting him a Saropa.
Subject: History of India

Questions: When was the Poona Pact transferred?
Explanation: On 24th September 1932, with the efforts of Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar and other Hindu leaders, Poona Pact was signed between upper caste Hindus and Dalits. According to this, the number of reserved seats for Dalits in the provincial legislature was increased from 71 to 148 and the number of reserved seats in the Central Legislature was increased by 18 percent.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The Justice Party in Madras made the experiment of dyarchy a success in the province because of their
Explanation: In the Government of India Act of 1919, communal representation and their reservations were not only allowed to remain but were substantially increased. The ease with which the British accepted the demand of the Justice Party (South Indian Liberal Federation) for reservation for non-Brahmins in Madras Province was quite suspicious. As a result, the popularity of the Justice Party increased and in the first elections under diarchy in 1920, the Justice Party won the majority. In this way, due to the anti-Brahmin stance of the Justice Party, the experiment of diarchy was successful in this province.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: Who among the following organized Vedaranyam Satyagraha in April 1930?
Explanation: When Gandhiji started the civil disobedience movement by violating the salt law from Dandi on 6 April 1930, Satyagraha to break the salt law started in the entire country. In the same sequence, in Madras province, C Rajagopalachari violated the salt law by traveling from Trichnapalli to Vedaranyam in April 1930.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: What can rightly said to be a very significant aspect of the Champaran Satyagraha?
Option A: Active all-India participation of lawyers, students and women in the National Movement
Option B: Active participation of Dalit and tribal communities of India in the National Movement
Option C: Joining of peasant unrest to India’s National Movement
Option D: Drastic decrease in the cultivation of plantation crops and commercial crops
Answer: (C) (C) Joining of peasant unrest to India’s National Movement
Explanation:
For the first time in the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 AD, the problem of farmers was raised at the national level and for the first time a national leader like Gandhiji supported the farmers to solve the problem.

The success of this movement increased the enthusiasm of the farmers and the farmers movement became uniquely associated with the national movement.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: Who wrote the book, ‘India Divided’?
Explanation: The book ‘India Divided’ was written by Dr. Rajendra Prasad which was published in 1946 AD. It contains a detailed explanation of the reasons behind the partition of India.
Subject: History of India

Questions: When was Mahatma Gandhi tried for the Champaran Satyagraha?

Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

Explanation: On 3 June, 1947, the Mount Batten Plan was announced which described the partition of India. It was first presented in the British Parliament on 4 July 1947. Explanation: The Indian Constituent Assembly was formed on 9 December 1946. Whose task was to create a separate constitution for India. The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into full force on 26 January 1950

Explanation: In the year 1902, a commission was formed under the chairmanship of Sir Raleigh. Explanation: Michael Madhusudan Dutt translated the Bengali play 'Neel Darpan' into English. This book was originally written in Bengali language, authored by Deenbandhu Mitra.

Questions: Who said, “A single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia”?

Explanation: In the year 1909, Punjab Hindu Sabha was established under the leadership of UN Mukherjee and Lalchand Sen. The main objective of establishing this assembly was to propagate the ancient ideas of Hindu religion and end the fundamentalist ideology.

Questions: Which one of the following places was famous as capital of Tipu Sultan
Explanation: The capital of Tipu Sultan was Srirangapatna. Srirangapatna became the capital of Mysore during the reign of Hyder Ali in the early 18th century. Tipu Sultan was a capable ruler, warrior as well as a famou scholar. Tipu Sultan ascended the throne of Mysore in 1782 AD and died in 1799 AD.

Explanation: The partition of Bengal was announced by Lord Curzon on 19 July 1905. Due to which a feeling of anger had arisen in the whole of Bengal. Questions: Who was the Prime Minister of England at the time of the Round Table Conference?
Explanation: The Round Table Conference i.e. the three Round Table Conferences were organized in 1930, 1931 and 1932 respectively. The Prime Minister of Britain at this time was Ramsay MacDonald. Questions: When was the capital of India changed from Calcutta to Delhi?
Explanation: Upon the arrival of British King George V in India in 1911, the partition of Bengal was canceled and it was announced that the capital of India would be transferred from Kolkata to Delhi. Explanation: “Pitt’s India Act” of 1784 was introduced by the British Parliament to bring the administration of the East India Company under the control of the British government. Questions: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of partition of Bengal in 1905 AD?
Explanation: The partition of Bengal was announced on 19 July 1905. At this time the Viceroy of India was Lord Curzon. This declaration of partition was implemented in the whole of Bengal from 16 October 1905. The declaration of this partition was cancelled by Lord Hardinge II.

Questions: Which of the following events brought fame to Mahatma Gandhi on his return to South Africa?
Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 in Gujarat. He went to South Africa in 1893 to work as a lawyer. Questions: Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand in-
Explanation: Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 AD. The main objective of establishing this society was to reform Hindu religion as a reaction to western influences. The book Satyarth Prakash written by Dayanand Saraswati is the basic text of Arya Samaj.

Questions: At which place was the first session of the Indian National Congress held in 1885?

Explanation: The revolution of 1857 started from Meerut on 10 May 1857. This revolution was the first expression of organized resistance against the British East India Company. This revolution in Bihar was led by Kunwar Singh.

Questions: World famous painting is found in which district of Bihar?
Explanation:
• The world famous Madhubani painting is also known as Mithila painting.
• This painting is famous for its vibrant colors, cultural themes and geometric patterns. The main themes of this painting are Hindu deities (Ram, Sita, Krishna, Durga etc.), nature, marriage and daily life.

• Natural colors are used in this painting. In this, paintings are made on walls, floors, clothes, canvas etc. with wooden pen, brush, finger, cloth, bamboo splint etc.
Bharni, Kachni, Tanik, Godna, Kohbar are the types of this painting. In the year 2007, Madhuban painting got GI (Geographical Indication) tag.

Questions: Where did the revolt of Birsa Munda take place ?
Explanation:
Birsa Munda Rebellion, also known as 'Ulgulan', was a major tribal rebellion led by Birsa Munda. This rebellion took place in the Chhotanagpur region (Jharkhand) between 1899-1900.
This rebellion started against the change of the traditional land system of the Mundas, Khuntkatt (collective farming) to Zamindari or individua land-ownership system.
The purpose of this rebellion was to protect the tribal rights against the unjust rule of the British and the landlords and religious, social atrocities.
• The main reasons for this rebellion were usurpation of tribal land, forced tax collection, conversion by Christian missionaries, restrictions on forest rights, etc.
The Munda tribe launched a rebellion against the British army and administration and armed conflict took place. Birsa Munda was arrested in 1900. He died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900.
• Result of the movement- Khuntkatti rights were recognized and forced labour was banned.
Subject: History of Bihar
