Questions: In the context of Indian handicrafts, what is 'Sujini' in Bihar?
Explanation:
• Sujani craft has a prominent place in the textile craft tradition of Bihar. Sujani craft was introduced for the use of infants after birth.

• Traditionally, Sujani is made by sealing pieces of old dhoti and saree together.
• The motherly feeling that one has towards the child comes down to it. By sewing two or three layers of dhoti or saree together, the cloth becomes stronger, then motifs are embroidered on these joined clothes by using straight, raw stitches.
• At present, there is a lot of variety in the base clothes of Sujani craft
• Now along with the old dhoti or saree, coloured, poplin, silk and marquin etc. are also being used.
Women use contrasting colours like orange, white, brown or yellow threads on red. Sujani's specialty is the depiction of common household matters, including flowers and plants.
• In this, the symbols of our religious faith, belief, affection, aspirations and ambitions are clearly visible.
• In ancient times, women of Bihar used to do Sujani work in their free time, but due to its attraction and excellence, this art has now become a source of income for women.
• For this reason it is being manufactured on a large scale. Danapur, Bhojpur and Muzaffarpur are its main manufacturing centers in Bihar.

the constitutional provisions, then on this basis State Emergency or President's Rule can be imposed in the State. The President may be satisfied on the basis of the Governor's report or otherwise.

According to Article 365, if a State is not following or is unable to follow the directions given by the Centre under Articles 256 and 257, then it will be legal for the President to conclude that the State Government cannot be run according to the constitutional provisions and it will be legal to make a proclamation under Article 356.

Singhvi 4. 1957 e. Balwant Rai Mehta 5. 1978 Code : (E) None of the above/More than one of the above 91. Which one of the following statements is correct regarding parliamentary form of Government?
Option A: The legislature is responsible to judiciary.
Option B: The legislature is responsible to executive.
Option C: The legislature and the executive are independent.
Option D: The President is responsible to the judiciary.
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: Parliamentary system is a system of democratic governance in which the executive derives its democratic legitimacy from the legislature and the executive is answerable to the legislature. In the parliamentary system, the executive and the legislature complement each other. The legislature is not answerable to the judiciary. It is answerable to the Legislative Assembly.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following was constituted under the Panchayati Raj system?
Explanation: Gram Panchayat has been created under the Panchayati Raj system. It is the lowest level of Panchayati Raj, which is the formalized form of local self-governance system in India at the village level. The Panchayati Raj system in India was started on 2 October 1959, the objective of which is to increase public participation in the process of development
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who amongst the following is the Land Records Officer?
Explanation: Patwari is appointed for the purpose of collection of land revenue from the farmers of a state and providing proper information to the government about the crops growing in a particular area. Patwari is a revenue officer who surveys agricultural lands in villages and maintains records of their ownership and holdings.
Subject: Geography

Questions: Which one of the following characteristics is not true for unitary form of government?
Explanation: The characteristics ideal for large countries are not suitable for centralized governance. Under unitary government, all authority and power is vested in one center, and there is no division of that power. In a unitary government there is only one government. Unitary government is ideal for small states. Whereas the federal form of government is beneficial for large countries marked by diversity.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Aam Aadmi Party is a–
Explanation:
Aam Aadmi Party was established on 2 October 2012 in New Delhi. This party is a type of state party. Which is recognized in Goa, Delhi and Punjab. Its registration is with the Election Commission. Conditions for recognition as a state level political party – The party must have secured 3 percent of the total seats in the state assembly elections or 3 seats, whichever is higher.

Or → In the Lok Sabha elections, a party must have won 1 seat out of every 25 Lok Sabha seats earmarked for the state.

Or → The party has secured 8 percent of the total valid votes in the elections held for the Lok Sabha or the Legislative Assembly in the state.

The answer given by the Commission is (E).
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which one of the following constitutional remedies is also called 'postmortem'?
Explanation:
A writ of certiorari is issued by a superior court to stop a subordinate court or judicial department from exceeding its jurisdiction. Writ of certiorari is also known as “postmortem”. By the Supreme Court and the High Court

A total of five types of writs are issued in the country, of which certiorari is the main one. Supreme Court Article. 32 and High Court Article. Issue writ under section 226.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which one of the following Indian states has the largest number of members in its state legislature?
Explanation:
Among the above options, Himachal Pradesh State Assembly has the highest number of members (68).

• Himachal Pradesh (68)

• Arunachal Pradesh (60)

• Manipur (60)

• Meghalaya (60)

Note – The state with the highest number of assembly seats in India is Uttar Pradesh (403).
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: In the Indian Order of Precedence, who amongst the following comes first?
Option D: The Chief Justice of the High Court
Explanation: According to the above options, the order of seniority of UPSC Chairman comes first. However, the Chairman, Comptroller and Auditor General and the Chief Election Commissioner are all at rank 9 (A). But among these three, the Chairman of UPSC comes first in priority. Apart from this, the order of precedence of various officials in the Indian polity is as follows –
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The 103<sup>rd</sup> Constitutional Amendment is related to
Explanation: The 124th Constitution Amendment Bill (103rd Amendment Act) was passed in the year 2019. This bill is related to 10% reservation in education and employment for the economically weaker sections of the general category. Gujarat is the first state in India to implement this bill.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: By how much has the number of members in the National Human Rights Commission been increased by the Human Rights Protection (Amendment) Act 2019?
Explanation: “National Human Rights Commission” was constituted in the year 1993. According to the amendment of the year 2019, in addition to the Chief Justice of India, a person who has been a judge of the Supreme Court can be appointed. At present Arun Kumar Mishra is the Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The name of the first Lokpal of India is
Explanation: The name of the first Lokpal of India is Pinaki Chandra Ghosh. Lokpal has been formed to hear complaints of corruption by government employees holding high positions and to prevent it. The Lokpal Act was passed by the Parliament in the year 2013. Present – Pradeep Kumar Mohanty
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The recently passed Triple Talaq Bill, 2019 provides for what maximum period of jail sentence?
Explanation: The Triple Talaq Bill was approved by the Union Cabinet in the year 2019 under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Under its rules and provisions, there is a provision of 3 years imprisonment for the accused person.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The provisions of Article 35-A and Article 370 were included in the Indian Constitution in-
Explanation: Article 35A was included in the Indian Constitution in the year 1954. Article 35A was a part of Article 370. At present, Article 370 has been abolished by passing “Jammu Kashmir Reorganization Bill 2019”.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Manipur state was formed in–
Explanation: Manipur state was established on 21 January 1972. Meghalaya and Tripura states were also formed in the year 1972. The capital of Manipur is Imphal and there are two Lok Sabha seats and one Rajya Sabha seat from here.
Subject: History of Bihar

Questions: The basis of judicial review in India is
Explanation: The Indian Constitution provides for judicial review through a procedure established by law. Under Article 137, the Supreme Court has the right to review its decisions. The Supreme Court also has the authority to exercise judicial superintendence over all the courts and panchayats of the country.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The President is elected in India by–
Option C: Members of both the houses of Parliament
Answer: (E) More than one of the above
Explanation: In India, the President is not elected directly by the people. The President is elected by an electoral college. They are elected through the single transferable system. The elected members of both the Houses of Parliament and the State Legislative Assemblies as well as the elected members of Delhi, J&K and Puducherry Legislative Assemblies are involved in the election of the President.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who presides over the joint session of Parliament?
Explanation: The joint session of Parliament is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha under Article 118. However, the President has the right to call this session. Till now joint session of Parliament has been held a total of three times.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: 1961 – Dowry Prohibition Bill 2. 1978 – Banking Services Bill 3. 2002 – Terrorism Prevention Bill 108. The executive power of the Union Government has been vested in–
Explanation: The entire executive powers of the Indian Union are vested in the President. The President has this right under Article 53(1). However, parliamentary system has been adopted in India. Therefore, the President is the executive in name only while the Prime Minister is the real executive. Article 74 provides for the formation of a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: On the basis of which constitutional amendment was Panchayati Raj given constitutional status?
Explanation:
The recommendation to give constitutional recognition to the Panchayati Raj system was made by the L.M. Singhvi Committee in 1986. It was given constitutional recognition by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment in 1992.

Panchayati Raj is described in Part 9, Schedule 11 and Article 243 of the Indian Constitution.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: In which political institution is place reserved for women in India?
Explanation: One-third (1/3) seats have been reserved for women in Panchayat elections. Article 243(D) of the Indian Constitution gives women the right to reservation in Panchayat elections. There are some states of India where women have 50% reservation in Panchayat, like – Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand etc.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The special election held to fill the vacancy in the legislature is called -
Explanation: The election which is conducted before time to fill the vacant seats in the legislature is called by-election. These elections are mostly held after the death or resignation of the members.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: At present the number of judges of the Supreme Court is
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: At present the number of judges in the Supreme Court including the Chief Justice has reached 34. Before the year 2019, this number was 31. The Supreme Court was established in the year 1950. Currently, as of September 2021, the Chief Justice is Dhananjay Yashwant Chandrachud.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Community development program started.
Explanation: The Community Development Program was started on 2 October 1952. It was started with the goals of comprehensive development in rural and urban areas of India.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: Who takes the decision to conduct Panchayat elections?
Explanation:
The decision to conduct Panchayat elections is taken by the state government. And the responsibility of conducting these elections rests with the State Election Commission. By the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, provision was made for State Election Commission to conduct Panchayat elections in every state.

64th BPSC
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: A Judge of the Supreme Court may resign his office by writing to–
Explanation: The tenure of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court is not clearly described in the Indian Constitution. But they can continue in their post till the age of 65 years. The Chief Justice resigns in the name of the President. At present (October 2021) the Chief Justice of India is N.V. Ramanna. Dhananjay Yashwant Chandrachud took over as the 50th Chief Justice on 9 November 2022.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who was the first Chairman of the Backward Classes Commission?
Explanation: The first Chairman of the first Backward Caste Commission was 'Kaka Saheb Kalelkar'. This commission was formed in 1953. The Chairman of the Second Backward Caste Commission was B.P. Mandal. The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) has been given constitutional status by the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act 2018. The National Backward Commission consists of five members. In which there is a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and three other members.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission is appointed by–
Option A: The Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
Explanation: The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission is appointed by the Governor of that State. But the Governor does not have the right to remove the Chairman of the Commission. The President has the right to remove it. Their tenure is 6 years or till the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: In order to be chosen a member of the Lok Sabha, a person must not be less than the age of–
Explanation: According to Article 84 (B), the minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 years and according to Article 173 (B), the minimum age to become a member of the State Assembly is also 25 years.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Age Limit for Lok Sabha Members

Questions: The Governor of a state is appointed by-
Option D: the Chief Justice of the High Cour
Explanation: The Governor of any state is appointed (Article 155) by the President. According to the suggestions of Sarkaria Commission (1983), “Before appointing a Governor in any state, advice should be taken from the Chief Minister of that state. This will promote Indian federalism.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: In which article of the Constitution of India was the provision for reservation of Scheduled Castes in the Lok Sabha made?
Explanation:
• According to Article 330 of the Indian Constitution, provision for reservation of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes has been made in the Lok Sabha
• Article 332 provides for reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in state assemblies
• At present, 84 and 47 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha respectively.
Subject: History of India

Questions: The President
Option A: is not a part of the Parliament
Option C: is a part of the Parliament and sits in the Parliament
Explanation: The Indian Parliament (Article 79) has three organs. President, Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha is called the upper house and Lok Sabha is called the lower house. In India, the President is considered the executive head of the Union.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which one of the following articles directs the State Governments to organized the Panchayat?
Explanation: Provision for formation of Panchayat has been made in Article 40 of the Indian Constitution. Panchayati Raj was given constitutional recognition by the 73rd amendment to the Constitution in the year 1992. The state government has the right to conduct Panchayat elections.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: In which one of the following years was Sarkaria Commission, which was empowered to recommend changes in Centre-State relations, submitted its report?
Explanation: The Sarkaria Commission dealing with Centre-State relations was constituted in 1983, which submitted its memorandum to the Central Government in October 1987. In its report, this commission had given many important suggestions to strengthen the federal structure.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Under which one of the following articles is the formation of Finance Commission laid down?
Explanation: There is a provision for the formation of Finance Commission under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution. This commission is constituted by the President. The main function of this commission is to divide revenue taxes between the Union and the States. Presently the Chairman of the 15th Finance Commission (2021-26) is NK Singh.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Attorney General of India is appointed by?
Option C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Explanation: Article 76 (1) of the Indian Constitution provides for the appointment of the Attorney General of India. They are appointed by the President. The Attorney General can participate in the proceedings of Parliament, but does not have the right to vote.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: After Independence, in which year were the Indian States reorganized on the linguistic basis?
Explanation:
On linguistic basis, “State Reorganization Commission was established in 1956 AD.” happened in. By the States Reorganization Act passed in 1956, 14 states and 6 union territories were formed on linguistic basis.

63th BPSC
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which one of the following committees/ commissions had recommended the creation of Nyaya Panchayats?
Explanation: Ashok Mehta Committee was established in 1977. This committee had recommended that Nyay Panchayat should be created as separate bodies from Development Panchayats and it should be headed by a qualified judge. Ashok Mehta Committee had also recommended making Panchayats two-tier.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Which one of the following functions is not the concern of local self government ?
Explanation: Maintenance of public discipline does not come under local self-government. Whereas public health, cleanliness, public utility services etc. come under it. Ripon is considered the father of local self-government in India.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The System of Panchayati Raj is mentioned in–
Explanation: Panchayati Raj system is a subject of the state list and the state government makes laws on all types of subjects related to it. At present there are 61 subjects under the state list. Agriculture, irrigation, roads, forests, district hospitals etc. come under the state list.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: 50% reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions is legalized in certain States such as– (i) Bihar (ii) Uttarakhand (iii) Madhya Pradesh (iv) Himachal Pradesh
Explanation: For the first time, Bihar state had made a provision of 50% reservation for women in Panchayat elections in the year 2006. At present, there are many states including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand which have given 50 percent reservation to women in Panchayats.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Reservation for Women in Panchayati Raj Institutions

Questions: Money Bill can be presented–
Option D: In joint meeting of both the Houses
Explanation: Money Bill is described in Article 110 of the Indian Constitution. These bills are introduced only in the Lok Sabha. This bill contains provisions related to the expenditure of the Consolidated Fund of India. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha takes the final decision on whether any bill is a money bill or not.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: What is the nature of the Indian Constitution?
Option D: Federal in nature but unitary in spirit
Answer: (D) (D) Federal in nature but unitary in spirit
Explanation: The Indian Constitution is considered federal in nature and unitary in spirit. But prominent constitutionalists have different opinions on this. According to Ambedkar the Indian Constitution is unitary and federal, according to the Supreme Court the Indian Constitution is federal. According to K. C. Wheare, the Indian Constitution is Quasi-federal.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who appoints the judges of the Supreme Court of India?
Explanation: Articles related to the appointment of judges of the Supreme Court are described in Article 124 (6) of the Indian Constitution. The judges of the Supreme Cour are appointed by the President.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
Explanation: The Vice President is described in Article 63 of the Constitution of India. Article 64 of the Constitution states that the Vice President will be the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Vice President is elected by an electoral college which includes members of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The Prime Minister of India is responsible to whom?
Explanation: The Prime Minister of India is collectively answerable to the Lok Sabha and personally answerable to the President. The Prime Minister has been discussed in Article 75 of the Constitution. He is usually the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: What is the minimum age for a Member of the Parliament?
Explanation: The Indian Parliament consist of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Article 84(B) of the Constitution states that to become a Lok Sabha member, the minimum age should be 25 years, while to become a Rajya Sabha member, the minimum age should be 30 years.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Minimum Age for Member of Parliament

Questions: What is the retirement age of judges of the Supreme Court?
Explanation: Under Article 124 (2) of the Constitution, the age of retirement of Supreme Court judges is 65 years. The judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Retirement Age of Supreme Court Judges

Questions: Who is the highest civil services officer of the Central Government?
Explanation:
In India, the Cabinet Secretary is the highest civil service officer in the Central Government. The Cabinet Secretary is the ex-officio head of all civil services under the Civil Services Board, Cabinet Secretariat, Indian Administrative Service.

60th -62nd BPSC
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which officer of the Government of India has the right to take part in the proceedings of Parliament of India even though he is not a member?
Explanation: The Attorney General is described in Article 76 of the Indian Constitution. The Attorney General is the highest legal officer of the country and has the right to participate in the proceedings of both the houses of the Parliament, but he does not have the right to vote during the proceedings of the Parliament.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Officer with Right to Participate in Parliament

Questions: Which of the following is/are listed among the Directive Principles given in Part IV of the Indian Constitution? (I) Equal pay for equal work (II) Uniform Civil Code (III) Small family norm (IV) Education through mother tongue at primar level
Explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy are included under Part IV of the Indian Constitution under Article 36–51. Article 39 talks about equal pay for equal work and Article 44 talks about a uniform civil code for citizens throughout the territory of India.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Vote on Account is meant for-
Option A: Vote on the report of CAG
Option C: Appropriating funds pending passing of budget
Answer: (C) (C) Appropriating funds pending passing of budget
Explanation: Vote on Account has been described in Article 116 of the Constitution. This is the account of revenue. Vote on Account helps the government to get money for expenditure till the full passage of the budget or for a short term expenditure. This is generally a part of the budget.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Constitution Day of India is celebrated on-
Explanation: Indian Constitution Day is celebrated every year on 26 November. The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into full force on 26 January 1950.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: A seat of a M.P. can be declared vacant if he/she absents himself from the house for a continuous period of–
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: If a member remains absent for more than a period of 60 days without the permission of the House, his post is declared vacant by the House. The thing to be noted here is that only if a member of the House is absent for 60 consecutive days, his post can be considered vacant.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The Supreme Court has held that hoisting the National Flag atop the private building is a fundamental right of every citizen under:
Explanation: Article 19 (1) (a) of the Indian Constitution gives every citizen of India the freedom to hoist the flag on their buildings and to express their views. On January 25, 2004, the Honorable Supreme Court said that hoisting the tricolor is a fundamental right of the citizens.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Choose the fundamental rights available to Indian Citizen but not to aliens– (I) Freedom of speech and expression (II) Equality before the law (III) Rights of minorities (IV) Protection of life and liberty
Option A: I and III (B) I and IV
Option C: II and IV (D) II and III
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation: Provision has been made for freedom of expression under Article 19 of the Constitution and protection of language and culture of minorities under Article 29. Both these rights are available only to Indian citizens. Non-Indian citizens do not have both these rights.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: The Panchayat Samiti formed at the block level in India is only a/an–
Explanation: Panchayat Samiti is considered the local unit of governance at the block level. Under the Panchayati Raj system of India, Panchayat Samiti functions as an administrative authority.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The expression ‘Socialist' was introduced in the Preamble of Indian Constitution by which amendment?
Explanation: Under the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, three new words socialism, secularism and integrity were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. The 42nd constitutional amendment was made in the year 1976 during the reign of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Match the following– (I) Union list (a) 97 entries (II) State list (b) 47 entries (III) Concurrent list (c) 66 entries Codes : I II III
Explanation: Union List, State List and Concurrent List are mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution. In which initially there were 97 subjects under the Union List, 66 subjects under the State List and 47 subjects under the Concurrent List. At present there are 100 subjects under the Union List, 61 subjects under the State List and 52 subjects under the Concurrent List.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Match the Lists – Union, State, Concurrent

Questions: Creation of a new state requires a________majority for Constitutional Amendment.
Option D: Two-thirds plus ratification by half of all states
Explanation: Under Article 3 of the Indian Constitution, Parliament has the right to establish new states. For this, the bill is passed by a simple majority of the members present in both the houses of the Parliament.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: President of India exercises his powers–
Option A: either directly or through officers subordinate to him
Answer: (A) (A) either directly or through officers subordinate to him
Explanation:
The President of India exercises his powers directly or through his subordinate officers. All executive power of the Indian Union is vested in the President but in reality these powers are exercised by the Prime Minister with the help of his cabinet.

56th -59th BPSC
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The Decentralization System was recommended by–
Explanation:
Democratic decentralization was recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee. This committee wa formed in 1957. He suggested making three-tier Panchayati Raj system

53rd -55th BPSC
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which one of the following human rights is also a fundamental right under the Indian Constitution?
Explanation: The right to education has been added to Article 21 (A) by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002. In this, children of 6 to 14 years of age were given the right to get free and compulsory education. Education has been made a fundamental right through the 86th Constitutional Amendment.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Human Rights – Also a Fundamental Right

Questions: When was the right to education added by amending the Indian Constitution?
Explanation: The Right to Education was added to Article 21(a) of the Indian Constitution under the 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002. This right to education was implemented all over India on 1 April 2010. Education is a subject of the concurrent list.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Right to Education – Added by Amendment

Questions: The Indian Constitution includes
Explanation: The Indian Constituent Assembly was established on 9 December 1946. The objective of which was to create a constitution to run the system of India smoothly. At present the Constitution of India is the largest written constitution in the world. The original Constitution had 395 articles, 22 parts and 8 schedules, but at present there are more than 450 articles, 22 parts and 12 schedules.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: How many members are in Rajya Sabha
Option A: 280 members, out of which 20 members are nominated by the President of India.
Option B: 275 members, out of which 18 members are nominated by the President of India.
Option C: 250 members, out of which 12 members are nominated by the President of India.
Option D: 252 members, out of which 12 members are nominated by the President of India.
Answer: (C) (C) 250 members, out of which 12 members are nominated by the President of India.
Explanation: The Parliament of India is formed by the joint membership of the President, Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha. In which Rajya Sabha is called the upper house and Lok Sabha is called the lower house. The maximum number of members in Rajya Sabha can be 250. Presently the number of members is 245, out of which 12 members are nominated by the President. Rajya Sabha was formed on 3 April 1952.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The decision to implement the Constitution on 26 January was taken because
Option A: Congress celebrated this date as Poorna Swaraj Day in 1930.
Option B: On this date in 1942, Quit India Movement was started.
Answer: (A) (A) Congress celebrated this date as Poorna Swaraj Day in 1930.
Explanation: The Indian Constitution was fully implemented on 26 January 1950. The date of 26 January was chosen because on this day in the year 1930, the Indian National Congress set the goal of complete independence for India and this day was celebrated as Independence Day.
Subject: History of India

Questions: Public Accounts Committee presents its report
Option A: To the Comptroller and Auditor General
Option B: To Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Option C: To the Minister of Parliamentary Affair
Answer: (B) (B) To the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Explanation: The Public Accounts Committee was constituted in 1921 under the Government of India Act 1919. Whose main function is to audit the expenses of the Government of India. There are a total of 22 member in this committee. In which 15 members are elected by the Lok Sabha and 7 members are elected by the Rajya Sabha. Public Accounts Committee is called the twin sister of the Estimates Committee. The Public Accounts Committee submits its report to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
Option A: Rajya Sabha is powerless in matters of wealth
Option B: Money Bill originates in Rajya Sabha.
Option C: Rajya Sabha has to pass bills within 14 days after they are passed by the Lok Sabha.
Option D: Rajya Sabha can pass a money bill or return it to the Lok Sabha with certain recommendatio--ns.
Answer: (B) (B) Money Bill originates in Rajya Sabha
Explanation:
Money Bill is defined in Article 110 of the Indian Constitution. Money Bill is introduced only in the Lok Sabha. The President cannot return this bill for reconsideration. A bill will be considered a money bil only if it contains provisions related to the following subjects.

• To deposit or withdraw something from the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund.
• Taking loan, regularizing or making any change in any right on behalf of the Government of India.
• To impose, reduce or make any change in tax.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following rights provided by the Indian Constitution is also available to noncitizens?
Option C: Freedom to move and settle in any part of the country
Explanation:
The right to constitutional remedies is also available to non-citizens. It has been described in Article 32 of the Constitution.

Article 32 has also been called the heart and soul of the Constitution.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who is the head of the National Security Committee?
Explanation: The advisor to the National Security Committee is the Prime Minister. It is a three-tier committee, which looks into security related matters. Under this, the post of National Security Advisor has been created, which is currently headed by Ajit Doval.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: According to which article 'National Emergency' can be declared by the President of India?
Explanation: Under Part 18 of the Constitution, emergency has been mentioned between Articles 352 – 360. In case of war or external attack, national emergency is imposed using Article 352. Till now, emergency has been imposed in India thrice in 1962, 1971, and 1975.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
Option A: The Supreme Court was formed in 1950
Option B: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the country, to which appeals are made.
Option C: The Supreme Court can hear any High Court/Courts other than the Court Martial.
Option D: The Supreme Court can hear courts-martial along with any other High Court/Courts
Answer: (C) (C) The Supreme Court can hear any High Court/Courts other than the Court Martial.
Explanation: The Supreme Court was formed on 26 January 1950. This is the highest court of the country. The Supreme Court has the authority to hear courts martial as well as any other high courts.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: Who is the constitutional head of the state governments?
Explanation: The Governor is the executive head of any state. All the powers of the state are vested in him, which he exercises with the help of the Cabinet headed by the Chief Minister. Constitutionally also the Governor is the head. Under Article 155, a Governor is appointed by the President in every state of the country. The role of the Governor has been described in Articles 153 to 162 of the Constitution.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Name the committee established by the NDC in 1957 for the reorganization of CDP and NES, which suggested a three-tier system of rural local government.
Explanation:
In the year 1957, Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was formed to strengthen the Panchayati Raj system. This committee gave the name of democratic decentralization to the Panchayati Raj system and they suggested a three-tier system for rural local governance, which is as follows-

• Village Panchayat
• Panchayat samiti
• District Council
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Ashok Mehta Committee recommended the following -
Explanation:
Ashok Mehta Committee was formed in December 1977. There were a total of 13 members in this committee. It submitted its report in the year 1978. This committee had suggested making the Panchayati Raj system twotier. It considered the district as the first level of decentralization in the state and talked about the formation of Mandal Panchayat below the district level. This committee had suggested abolition of Gram Panchayat and Panchayat Samiti.

Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: A Bill which is presented in the Parliament becomes an Act after which action?
Option A: When it is passed by both the houses of the Parliament.
Option B: When the President gives his consent.
Option C: When the Prime Minister signs it.
Option D: When the Supreme Court declares it to be within the jurisdiction of the Central Parliament.
Answer: (B) (B) When the President gives his consent.
Explanation: A bill is considered enacted when it is passed in both the houses of the Parliament (Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha) and after that if the President assents to that bill then that bill becomes an Act.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: According to our Constitution, the tenure of the Rajya Sabha is –
Answer: (D) (D) It is not subject to disolution
Explanation: Rajya Sabha is mentioned in Article 80 of the Indian Constitution. Rajya Sabha is called the Upper House. One third of its members retire every two years. Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: A High Court Judge addresses his resignation letter to-
Option C: Chief Justice of the High Court of his state
Explanation: A judge of any High Court addresses his resignation letter to the President. High Court judges can hold their post till the age of 62 years. Judges in the High Courts are appointed by the President of India after consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the concerned State.
Subject: Society

Questions: A person may take part in the proceedings of either House of Parliament as a non-member -
Explanation: The Attorney General of India is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India. The Attorney General has been mentioned in Article 76 of the Indian Constitution. The Attorney General has the right to participate in the proceedings of both the Houses, but he does not have the right to vote in the House if necessary. The Attorney General is appointed by the President.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: By which constitutional amendment have the fundamental duties been added to the Constitution of India?
Explanation: The Fundamental Duties were added to Part – 4 (a) of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976 on the recommendation of Sardar Swaran Singh. Initially there were 10 fundamental duties, but at present there are 11 fundamental duties
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: How many languages are recognized as scheduled languages in the Indian Constitution?
Explanation: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with language. Initially 14 languages were included in this schedule, but at present 22 languages are included in this schedule
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: Consider the following words. (1) Socialist (2) Democratic (3) Sovereign (4) Secular Arrange the correct words according to the idea.
Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution has been called the essence of the Constitution. The word mentioned in it are – sovereign, socialist, secular democratic

• Prominent constitutionalist K.M. Munshi ha called the Preamble the key to the Constitution
Subject: General Mental Ability & CSAT

Questions: In which House the presiding officer is not a member of that House?
Explanation: The Vice President has been mentioned in Article 63 of the Constitution. The Vice President serves as the exofficio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Even though the Vice President is not a member of the Rajya Sabha, he presides over that house. In this situation his powers are equivalent to those of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Article 64 states that the Vice President will be the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: By which Constitution Amendment Act the voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
Explanation: By the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act in 1989, Article 326 of the Constitution was amended and the voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years. The right to vote is a statutory right in India.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: If the posts of President and Vice President are vacant then who holds the post of President of India?
Explanation: In the absence of the President and Vice President, the Chief Justice of India holds the office of President. It has been mentioned in the Constitution that if the President is absent then the Vice President will take over his charge but if the Vice President is also absent then in such a situation the Chief Justice of India will take over that charge.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: There is a Panchayat Samiti on a development block –
Explanation: Panchayat Samiti is an administrative authority on the development block. There is a Panchayat Samiti in each block, which is also named after the same block.
Subject: Bihar Polity & Governance

Questions: The Prime Minister of India is head of-
Explanation: According to Article 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President. The Prime Minister is the actual head of the executive who acts as a bridge between the President and the Council of Ministers. Just as the Prime Minister is the head of the Central Government, similarly the Chief Minister is the head of the State Government.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who among the following has been given the power to enforce fundamental rights by the Constitution?
Option A: To all the courts of India
Explanation: Under Part-III of the Indian Constitution, fundamental rights have been mentioned between Articles 12-35. Parliament has the right to enforce the fundamental rights in the Constitution, while in case of its violation, both the Supreme Court and the High Court have the right to hear it. Under Article 32 and Article 226, a person can go to the Supreme Court and High Court respectively for hearing in case of violation of his rights.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: By whom can the President of India be removed?
Option C: By the Chief Justice of India
Explanation: The President of India can be removed through impeachment if he violates the Constitution. It is necessary to inform the President 14 days before impeachment. There is a provision for impeachment of the President under Article 61 of the Indian Constitution. The motion of impeachment can be brought in any house of the Parliament.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following subjects is in the concurrent list?
Explanation: The Central List, State List and Concurrent List are described in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution. Under the Concurrent List, the common rights of both the State Government and the Central Government have been described. At present there are a total of 52 subjects under this list. Education, labor welfare, newspapers, forests, family planning etc. come under the concurrent list.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who was the chairman of the committee on whose recommendation Panchayati Raj was established in India?
Explanation: Panchayati Raj was established in India on the recommendation of Balwant Rai Mehta Committee. This committee was formed in 1957. This committee had talked about the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system. In the year 1993, the Panchayati Raj system was given constitutional status through the 73rd and 74th constitutional amendments.
Subject: Indian Economy

Questions: State-wise allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha is based on the 1971 census. Till how many years will this determination remain the same?
Explanation: On the basis of the 1971 census, state-wise allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha was made till the year 2000 by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment 1976. But through the 84th Constitutional Amendment in 2001, it has been extended to 2026.
Subject: Current Affairs

Questions: Panchayati Raj system in India was first introduced in Rajasthan and ____
Explanation: In the year 1958, the National Development Council accepted the recommendations of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee and on 2 October 1959, the country's first three-tier Panchayat was inaugurated by the then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh.
Subject: Current Affairs

Questions: How many members are nominated by the President in Rajya Sabha?
Explanation: Under Article 80(3) of the Indian Constitution, a person who has done notable work in the field of literature, art, social service, science is nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the President. Article 80 of the Indian Constitution deals with the constitution of Rajya Sabha. The maximum number of seats in Rajya Sabha can be 250 but at present this number is 245.
Subject: Bihar Polity & Governance

Questions: By whom is the decision taken for holding Panchayat elections?
Explanation: The decision to conduct Panchayat elections is taken by the state government. The term of Gram Panchayat is 5 years. It is mandatory to organize Gram Panchayat meeting at least once in two months. The structure o Gram Panchayat includes head, deputy head and ward members. Panchayat was given constitutional status under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India is related to the freedom of the press?
Explanation: Article 19 of the Indian Constitution talks about 6 types of freedom. According to this article, the citizens of India have been given freedom of speech, thought and expression. Freedom of the press is not mentioned separately in the Constitution. This comes under the freedom of expression guaranteed by Article 19(A).
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Act was called Mini Constitution?
Explanation: The 42nd amendment of the Constitution is called Mini Constitution. The 42nd constitutional amendment was made in 1976. This amendment is also important from the point of view that through this amendment the words socialism, secularism and integrity were added to the Preamble. This amendment was made during the Emergency (25 June 1975 to 21 March 1977).
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Who appoints the Governor of Jammu and Kashmir?
Option A: Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir
Option B: Chief Justice of Jammu and Kashmir High Court
Explanation:
In Jammu and Kashmir, the Governor is appointed by the President. The Governor is the head of the executive of the state. The Governor acts as a bridge between the state and the Centre. The post of Governor is very important for promoting Indian federalism.

Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following describes India as a secular state?
Explanation: The words socialism, secularism and integrity were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976. India is a secular country. That is, India has an equal view towards all religions.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Right to constitutional remedies comes under what?
Explanation: Fundamental rights have been described in Articles (12 – 35) under Part – III of the Indian Constitution. In which Article – 32 provides constitutional remedies against violation of fundamental rights. Baba Saheb Ambedkar had called Article 32 the soul of the Constitution.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which article of the Constitution of India recognizes Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union?
Explanation: Articles 343 to 351 of the Indian Constitution describe the official language. According to Article 343(1) of the Constitution, the official language of the Indian Union is Hindi and the script is Devanagari. Hindi was accepted as the official language of India on 14 September 1949.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Firstly, for what period can the declaration of emergency be limited?
Explanation: Article 352 of the Constitution mentions emergency in case of external aggression. Once the declaration of emergency is approved by the Parliament, the emergency can be imposed for a period of six months.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Period for which declaration of emergency can be limited

Questions: By whom is the Chief Minister of a Union Territory where such a provision exists, appointed?
Explanation: In those union territories where there is a provision for the post of Chief Minister, the Chief Minister is appointed by the President. At present the post of Chief Minister is created in the Union Territory of Delhi and Puducherry.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Appointment of Chief Minister of a Union Territory

Questions: Who controls the expenditure of the Parliament of India?
Explanation: The expenditure of the Parliament of India is controlled by the “Comptroller and Auditor General”. (CAG) has been mentioned in Article 148 of the Constitution. CAG submits its annual report to the President.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Control of expenditure of the Parliament

Questions: The concept of Public Interest Litigation originated from which country?
Explanation: The concept of Public Interest Litigation in India has been taken from America. Public interest litigation works on public interest sentiments. PN Bhagwati has an important contribution in starting Public Interest Litigation in India. PIL compels the executive and legislature to perform their constitutional duties and also ensures corruption-free administration.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: Which of the following writs are applicable against illegal detention of a person?
Explanation: A writ of habeas corpus is issued against the illegal detention of a person. It is mandatory for the person detained by this writ to be physically produced before the court within 24 hours.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Applicability of writs against illegal detention

Questions: In which of the following is the provision for amendment of the constitutional provision made?
Explanation: Constitutional amendment has been mentioned in Article 368 under Part XX of the Indian Constitution. This form of amendment has been included in the Constitution of India from the Constitution of South Africa.
Subject: Indian Polity

Questions: The Supreme Commander of the Indian Defense Force is
Option A: Chief of Army Staff of the Indian Arm
Explanation: The President is the commander-in-chief of all three armies of India – Army, Air Force and Navy. However, the President appoints a chief in each forces to run the operations of these three forces smoothly.
Subject: Indian Polity
Subtopic: Supreme Commander of the Indian Defense Force

Questions: Who is the executive head of the state government?
Explanation:
The executive head of the state government is the Governor. The state executive consists of the Chief Minister along with the Governor and the Council of Ministers. The Governor discharges constitutional functions in the state such as appointing the Chief Minister and taking decisions regarding matters relating to assent to any bill passed by the legislature.

Questions: Which of the following is called the 'Soul' of the Indian Constitution?

The day when it is the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere is the same day when it is the shortest day in the Southern Hemisphere. Similarly, this change is also seen in the Southern Hemisphere. Questions: Which of the following atmospheric features is associated with the performance of the Indian summer monsoon?
Answer: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
Explanation:
Atmospheric features like tropical easterly jet stream, shifting of ITCZ (Inter Tropical Conversion Zone) etc. influence the Indian summer monsoon. Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) refers to a low pressure area or belt where winds from high air pressure areas come and converge. The pre-summer ITCZ belt is formed in the Indian Ocean. North-eastern trade winds blow towards this low pressure area. Due to passing through the Indian landmass, these winds get heated due to which the low pressure center in the Indian landmass becomes deeper. This north-eastern trade wind is also called eastern jet stream. After reaching the Indian Ocean, these winds cool down and develop high air pressure. In summer, when the ITCZ belt reaches near 25°N over the Indian landmass, a strong low pressure center develops here.

While there is a strong high pressure condition in the Indian Ocean region, from this high pressure region, moist winds move from the SW direction and reach the Indian mainland, which is called SW monsoon. Although the summer monsoon in India first arrives in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Questions: The ratio of total deposits that a Commercial Banks must keep with Reserve Bank of India is called
Explanation:
Legal Reserve Ratio (LRR) is a ratio in which commercial banks are required to keep a certain part of their total deposits as reserve, as per the rules of the Reserve Bank of India. This ratio is divided into two parts.

(i) Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)
(ii) Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)

• Cash Reserve Ratio is the minimum percentage that all commercial banks have to deposit a certain part of their total deposits (Net Demand and Time Liability (NDTL)) as cash with the Reserve Bank of India.
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio is the minimum percentage of Net Demand and Time Liability (NDTL) that every commercial bank has to keep with itself in the form of liquid cash, gold or government securities.
